record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Let Sfin(Ω, Ω) mean that for every sequence of open ω-covers of a set of reals X one can choose finitely many members from each cover so that all chosen sets together still form an open ω-cover. Does ZFC prove the existence of a set of reals with Sfin(Ω, Ω) and cardinality d?

evidence.quote: Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals satisfying Sfin(Ω, Ω) such that |X| = d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the real line with its standard topology, and let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$. An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is called an $\omega$-cover of $X$ if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and for every finite subset $F \subseteq X$ there exists $U \in \mathcal{U}$ with $F \subseteq U$. Let $\Omega(X)$ denote the family of all open $\omega$-covers of $X$.

The selection principle $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega,\Omega)$ holds for $X$ if for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\omega}$ with $\mathcal{U}_n \in \Omega(X)$, there exist finite subsets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n\in\omega} \mathcal{F}_n \in \Omega(X)$.

Let $\mathfrak{d}$ denote the dominating number, namely the least cardinality of a family $D \subseteq \omega^\omega$ such that for every $f \in \omega^\omega$ there exists $g \in D$ with $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

Question: Does ZFC prove the existence of a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ satisfying $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega,\Omega)$ with $|X| = \mathfrak{d}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surfaced surveys of selection-principle open problems (including the Tsaban milestone of open problems and follow-up work on $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega,\Omega)$), but no source was found that explicitly resolves whether ZFC alone produces a set of reals satisfying $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega,\Omega)$ of cardinality $\mathfrak{d}$. The problem appears to still be regarded as open, but verification was inconclusive.
